slides.title: Meta's Muse Spark Small (under 100 Bln params)
slides.text: Meta's Muse Spark Small (under 100 Bln params) - yet competes with huge models ( ~ Trillion params). How is it even possible? 1. Meta completely rebuilt its pretraining stack from scratch, achieving the same capability as larger models using over 10× less compute 2. "Thought compression" trained via reinforcement learning helps to solve problems with far fewer reasoning tokens, making it dramatically faster 3. Multiple (16) small (70B) agents reasoning in parallel ("Contemplating mode") - cutting latency without sacrificing quality (16*70B = 1.12T params) Combined with native multimodal architecture, these engineering choices prove that smarter design beats raw parameter count — efficiency, not size, is the new frontier. https://ai.meta.com/blog/introducing-muse-spark-msl/ Meta - Muse Spark From Llama to Muse Name "Muse" - creative assistance and deep personalization "Spark" - entry-level model, fast Developed internally as "Project Avocado"

slides.title: Matthew Berman discusses the alarming rise of AI-powered
slides.text: Matthew Berman discusses the alarming rise of AI-powered cyberattacks, highlighting Google’s recent discovery of the first AI-generated zero-day exploit used in the wild He explains that AI is dramatically increasing the velocity and sophistication of threats, such as widespread supply chain worms and highly realistic deepfake phishing attempts However, he argues that the ultimate solution is an "AI arms race" where superior defensive models, like OpenAI’s GPT-5.5 Cyber and Anthropic’s Mythos, harden systems faster than attackers can breach them While large organizations can afford this top-tier protection, Berman warns that individuals face increased risk because AI makes low-value, high-volume attacks more profitable Ultimately, he stresses that national security depends on maintaining a lead in AI development to outpace adversarial state actors . https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5H3LGJSyaHM AI Cyber Attacks Google Says Hackers Used AI to Build Zero-Day Exploit https://www.techrepublic.com/article/news-google-hackers-ai-zero-day-exploit/ By early 2026, the use of LLMs and autonomous agents in security research has moved from experimental labs to finding hundreds of real-world vulnerabilities While LLMs are frequently used to "triage" existing bugs, a subset of CVEs has been attributed directly to AI-assisted discovery or specifically identified within AI frameworks by other AI agents.

slides.title: Suprmind AI Hallucination Hub https://suprmind.ai/hub/ai-hallucination-rates-and-benchmarks/ BridgeBench Hallucination Leaderboard
slides.text: Suprmind AI Hallucination Hub https://suprmind.ai/hub/ai-hallucination-rates-and-benchmarks/ BridgeBench Hallucination Leaderboard https://www.bridgebench.ai/hallucination Vectara Leaderboard on Hugging Face https://www.vectara.com/blog/introducing-the-next-generation-of-vectaras-hallucination-leaderboard Reasoning/thinking models consistently score worse on Vectara's harder new dataset than non-reasoning models - GPT-5, Claude Sonnet 4.6, Grok-4, and DeepSeek-R1 all exceed 10%, while the non-reasoning Gemini 2.5 Flash-Lite sits at just 3.3%. This is counterintuitive - "thinking more" appears to introduce more fabrication in summarization tasks, possibly because extended reasoning generates more text that strays from the source https://www.mayhemcode.com/2026/04/vectara-hallucination-leaderboard.html Hallucination Leaderboards Reducing RAG hallucinations: 1. clean your knowledge base, remove duplicates, outdated content, and use 300–500 token chunks with metadata 2. improve retrieval with hybrid search (dense + BM25), a cross-encoder reranker, and query expansion 3. strengthen prompts: set temperature to 0, explicitly allow "I don't know," and require the model to cite verbatim quotes before composing answers 4. add an output verification step - a second LLM-as-judge call or semantic similarity check to catch claims not grounded in retrieved context For quick wins: temperature=0, a reranker, and an LLM judge are the highest-impact

slides.title: Agentic RAG - uses a loop with LLM
slides.text: Agentic RAG - uses a loop with LLM and tools to search, read, and self-correct until it finds the correct information https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=RxwjoegpI98 List Files, Grep (regex search) - returning line numbers and context PydanticAI - helps to connect tools to an LLM The Loop: The agent first lists files, then uses the "grep" tool to find mentions of a topic, and finally reads the most relevant files to formulate an answer Visibility - streaming steps, debugging to see exactly which tool parameters the LLM is choosing Structured Output (Pydantic model) - agent returns a clean JSON object containing the answer and specific citations (file name, quote, and line number) Improvement - use ripgrep (rg) - better and faster Safety Guards - request limits and maximum line-read constraints Error Handling - return human-readable error messages - allows the LLM to understand what went wrong and try a different approach Agentic RAG is more expensive and has higher latency than semantic RAG, but it is far more accurate for complex queries over private documentation because the agent can "think" and refine its search strategy dynamically Agentic RAG

slides.title: A Better, Cheaper RAG - (Neuro-Sym Multi-hop Reasoning)
slides.text: A Better, Cheaper RAG - (Neuro-Sym Multi-hop Reasoning) http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=CLjTCe_cvJs TGS-RAG - bidirectional, makes RAG both more accurate and significantly cheaper Combines text search with knowledge graphs "orphan entity bridging" - saves pruned graph nodes in a memory buffer If a parallel text search identifies a discarded node as relevant, the path is instantly "resurrected" without new database queries This approach achieves superior local accuracy while using 80% less compute and drastically reducing token costs compared to industry standards like GraphRAG https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=CLjTCe_cvJs A Better, Cheaper RAG Meta’s Super Intelligent Retrieval Agent (SIRA) RAG SIRA replaces multi-step agentic loops with a precise, one-shot mathematical approach SIRA uses expanded BM25 lexical search instead of vector embeddings It works by using an LLM to predict "expected response sketches" for queries and pre-expanding document indices with latent synonyms This allows the system to capture fine-grained technical jargon often lost in vector compression Benchmarks show significant accuracy gains over current models, critics highlight high offline compute costs and a heavy reliance on the LLM’s internal knowledge cutoff SIRA aims to transform information retrieval into a deterministic, expert-level action rather than a stochastic search process. https://github.com/facebookresearch/sira https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gxbp3BUo3wk

slides.title: Hermes Agent and Pareto Code Hermes Agent acts
slides.text: Hermes Agent and Pareto Code Hermes Agent acts as a persistent "brain" that remembers past interactions and builds custom skills Pareto Code, an experimental router from Open Router , automatically selects the most effective coding model (such as Claude or Gemini) based on task complexity The system manages project memory and scheduling while ensuring the best available model handles technical execution This setup eliminates decision fatigue and allows for cross-device continuity and sophisticated automation https://openrouter.ai/openrouter/pareto-code https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kQHi_dXugbI AI Updates Hermes "computer use" on MacOS Autonomously operate a Mac desktop - clicking, typing, and scrolling - entirely in the background without interrupting the user's active workflow The agent uses vision-based screenshot analysis to navigate the screen and supports multiple AI models, including Claude, GPT-4, Gemini, and local models Multi-layer safety guardrails require user approval for sensitive actions like file deletion In demos, Hermes handled simple tasks well, such as creating notes and even spawning a second instance of itself, but struggled with complex workflows like organizing an Obsidian knowledge base

slides.text: $80M in 6 Months With No Team (New Startup Playbook) In 2026, the traditional barriers to starting a company (technical co-founders, capital, and long runways) have collapsed AI now enables individuals to build prototypes in days, while lean methodology allows for validation without outside investment This shift has created the "Founder Economy," where the primary advantage is ownership of a business model rather than just an audience or gig However, this accessibility creates a new trap: the ability to build the wrong thing 10x faster Because execution is now cheap, the new bottleneck is problem clarity To succeed, "latent founders" with deep domain expertise must prioritize customer validation and small experiments over immediate building to ensure they are solving a problem people will actually pay for. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KO7MxL6bKj4 AI Updates Ash Maurya

slides.title: Companies Are Re-hiring Developers https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6aTNBCqm3zE In 2023, tech
slides.text: Companies Are Re-hiring Developers https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6aTNBCqm3zE In 2023, tech companies began massive layoffs switching to AI Companies soon discovered that AI-generated code produced nearly twice as many errors, created 38% more code to maintain, and reduced real productivity by 50% The core issue was that AI lacked understanding of system context, architecture decisions, and complex integrations Debugging AI-generated code became extremely time-consuming By 2026, companies began quietly rehiring developers, often the same people they had laid off, through "boomerang hiring." The industry realized that understanding systems, debugging, and making informed architectural decisions are the valuable skills that AI cannot yet replicate effectively Companies Are Re-hiring Developers

slides.title: Julia McCoy argues that LinkedIn is broken due
slides.text: Julia McCoy argues that LinkedIn is broken due to pay-to-play promotions, ghost jobs (30–50% of listings), and companies bypassing aggregators entirely The job market has three layers: the visible market (high competition on LinkedIn/Indeed), an aggregated market of 400,000+ scraped listings and a hidden market of direct corporate postings AI tool JobRight surfaces these hidden roles hours before they hit LinkedIn, with under 25 applicants. McCoy predicts LinkedIn loses dominance by end of 2026, AI agents handle first-round interviews by mid-2027, and traditional job searching is replaced by continuous AI-to-AI matching by late 2027 https://jobright.ai JobRight.AI
